completed_tasks: NEX-105 CSRF origin guard - VERIFIED. Cookie-authenticated unsafe requests must come from our own origin or a CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS entry. Product afd07e1, docs 91173bf, CI 46174865205 green end to end. 32 test cases measured from collection; wiring proved load-bearing by unregistering the middleware (exactly the 4 wired-app tests went red).
Registered the guard in bootstrap/app.py AFTER CORSMiddleware so it runs BEFORE it (Starlette runs last-added first), so a forged write is refused by the guard rather than answered by the CORS layer.

Added CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS to Settings with the same NoDecode/comma-separated validator treatment as cors_allow_origins, deliberately independent of CORS: a permissive read list must not become a write permission.

Wrote 32 cases in tests/authentication/test_csrf_origin_guard.py -- measured by pytest collection, not counted from source -- covering the pure evaluate() rule and the wired app (foreign-origin refusal, same-origin success, missing-Origin refusal, bearer unaffected, safe read served, foreign-origin logout refused, no CORS header echoed on refusal).

Proved the wiring load-bearing: unregistering the middleware turned exactly the four wired-app tests red and left the pure-function cases green. That split is the evidence that the rule is reachable from HTTP and not merely correct in isolation.

Fixed two pre-existing logout tests that the guard correctly broke (403 not 204): TestClient sends no Origin, so the tests now send Origin like a real browser. The alternative -- exempting /auth/logout -- was rejected because it is the one route that most needs the check.

Corrected docs/SECURITY.md, which still claimed CSRF was 'not applicable: the API is token/header-based, not cookie-based'. That sentence became false when session cookies shipped and is now replaced with the enforced rule, the fail-closed cases, and the stated residual.

risks: NEX-105's CI is unread. The local gates are green and the mutation control is measured, but a local green is not a CI green -- the migration step and the frontend jobs do not run locally in the same shape. NEX-105 is PUSHED, not VERIFIED, and promoting it before reading the verdict would be the exact falsification the status legend forbids.

The guard is origin-based, not token-based, so a non-browser cookie client that omits Origin is now refused rather than served. That is the intended direction of failure and is documented, but it is a real behaviour change for such a client and the first thing to check if an integration breaks after this slice.

Shell multi-line `-m` commit messages are corrupted on this host -- hit again this run (the body self-interleaved and repeated; caught only by reading `git log -1 --format=%B` back). The content was unaffected and the message was repaired via file_editor + `commit --amend -F`. This is the same family as the documented heredoc trap: write the text to a file with file_editor, then pass `-F`. Never assume a multi-line `-m` landed intact.

This clone is shallow/grafted and its fetch refspec maps only main. merge-base, `branch -r --contains` and `git rev-parse origin/<branch>` all read one unrefreshed cache and can agree on a wrong hash. Use `git ls-remote` for the head, and fetch explicitly into a temp ref before inspecting remote content.

decisions_this_run: Put the CSRF check in middleware rather than in the authentication dependency, because POST /auth/logout reads the session cookie without resolving a Principal. A dependency-level guard would have left that route unprotected and, worse, silently so, since a missing dependency produces no error. The middleware also covers routes added later -- the same reasoning that produced NEX-100 and NEX-101.

Made CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS a separate setting from CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS rather than reusing it. CORS is a read barrier the browser enforces; making 'trusted to read' imply 'trusted to write' would mean any permissive development CORS list silently became a write permission. Two settings mean widening one cannot widen the other, and an empty value means same-origin only rather than allow-everyone.

Fixed the two failing logout tests by making them send Origin, not by exempting /auth/logout from the guard. The guard was right and the tests were unrealistic -- TestClient is not a browser. Weakening a control to keep a test green is precisely the failure the operating rules forbid, and /auth/logout is the route that most needs the check.

Kept the decision logic as a pure function (evaluate) returning a verdict plus a reason, with the middleware as a thin parsing adapter. This made the rule testable without an app, and made the mutation control meaningful: unregistering the middleware left the pure tests green and turned only the four wiring tests red, which is how the wiring was shown to be load-bearing rather than decorative.

Held NEX-105 at PUSHED rather than promoting it to VERIFIED, and did not open a PR. Both follow from the same fact -- the CI verdict was unread when the window closed. Local gates passing is not a CI verdict, and a PR is only warranted when a reviewer has validated work to act on, not when work merely exists.

Corrected a number I had first asserted from source (30 test cases) to the measured figure (32), then rewrote the BACKLOG entry around it. A count read off the file is a guess; a collection run is evidence.
